answer: SWEBOK v4.0a does not limit maintenance to just post-delivery. The guide defines maintenance as activities required for cost-effective support of software in operation, performed in both pre-delivery and post-delivery stages. It cites ISO/IEC/IEEE 14764, stating the objective of software maintenance as modifying existing software while preserving its integrity. However, the evidence shows that the ISO text itself is metadata-only and was not independently inspected in this project. Therefore, the scope of maintenance as defined in SWEBOK v4.0a includes pre-delivery activities, not just post-delivery. The limitations noted for SWEBOK v4.0a include it being a guide to the body of knowledge, not the complete body of knowledge, and not all related disciplines being characterized in full.
